title: Meditation
body: A serverless API that generates embeddable SVG stat cards for GitHub profiles. Built with Hono and deployed on Vercel. Inspired by manhwa titles and stoic philosophy.

star.situation: I depended on an external GitHub stats generator for my profile, but it frequently went down or became unreliable. The dependency introduced uncertainty into something that should remain stable.
star.task: Build a self-controlled, serverless API that generates GitHub stat cards reliably, with predictable performance and full ownership over behavior and design.
star.action: I designed a minimal API using Hono, separating concerns between data fetching, caching, SVG generation, and theming. I implemented in-memory caching to reduce repeated GitHub API calls, structured endpoints for clarity, and ensured each response is deterministic. The system was built to remain simple, observable, and easy to maintain.
star.result: The system no longer depends on external availability. Stat cards are consistently accessible, performance remains stable under normal load, and failures are contained within a system I control. Reliability replaced convenience.

technicalFailures.title: Single-Source Assumption
technicalFailures.what: I relied too heavily on a single source when studying GitHub API patterns and related protocols like gRPC, which led to misunderstandings in implementation and unnecessary complexity in early iterations.
technicalFailures.why: I assumed one well-written documentation source was sufficient. I did not cross-reference or validate concepts across multiple perspectives, which caused gaps in understanding.
technicalFailures.lesson: Documentation is a map, not the territory. Read broadly, compare sources, and verify through implementation.
